## Purpose

This report documents my rough-draft progress for **Qualtrics M01-1: Designing a Survey**. The assignment asks students to convert the Word version of the *Survey of Educational Needs for MR Professionals* into a Qualtrics survey, reflect question numbers, recode values, skip/display logic, and improve the survey's presentation. The module specifically states that this checkpoint is a **rough draft** and that the survey does not need to be complete yet.

## Work completed

I created the Qualtrics project using the required naming format:

**Huang, Yushan - Survey of Educational Needs of MR Professionals**

I then built the beginning portion of the survey through **Q2.11**. The rough-draft work completed so far includes:

- **Q1.1** – consent/introduction question with Yes/No responses, recode values **1 = Yes** and **2 = No**, and skip logic sending **No** to the end of the survey.
- **Q1.2** – market-research experience question with Yes/No responses and skip logic sending **No** to the end of the survey.
- **Q2.1** – Part 1 section introduction.
- **Q2.2-Q2.10** – employment, company, occupation, organizational-level, and job-role questions, including recode values and text entry for applicable “Other” choices.
- **Q2.11** – matrix question with 12 research-activity rows and four response columns. The response recodes are **3 = Primary function, 2 = Secondary function, 1 = Not part of job role, and 9 = Do not know**.

## Reflection on the work completed so far

The rough-draft process helped me become more familiar with building survey questions in Qualtrics and matching a source questionnaire's structure. I practiced selecting different question types, setting single-answer response formats, adding text entry to applicable “Other” choices, assigning recode values, applying skip logic, and using the preview function to visually check the survey.

At this stage, the survey is intentionally **not complete**, consistent with the module's instruction that the rough draft may contain only part of the final survey. The completed portion currently reaches Q2.11.
